title: RAW UNREVIEWED: a Yacea remedy branch changes recipient class while retaining the herb
summary: The recorded 1485 Gart der Gesundheit Yacea chapter lead describes a child-specific porridge or herb-water use alongside other applications of the same named plant. Verify the complete chapter primary, including the exact recipient, preparation, condition and clause order; freeze a same-herb/different-recipient graph before considering an admitted Herbal target. A whole f9v proposal would have to distinguish that child recipient branch from generic herb preparation and from another patient's route while preserving the same plant referent across its two paragraphs. This is a narrower relation than simply finding a plant name or two administration routes. No f9v child term, paragraph alignment or source-to-manuscript identity is claimed; missing independent target recipient ownership ends at capacity review.

design.mechanism: one source-named plant persists across a treatment branch whose patient class is restricted to children
design.unit: complete 1485 Gart Yacea chapter after primary verification and the complete admitted f9v two-paragraph entry
design.contrast: child-specific recipient branch versus an unqualified preparation list for the same herb
design.prediction: a frozen whole reading retains one herb owner and binds the child-only recipient and its preparation to one branch without assigning that restriction to the other branch; no independently owned target recipient gives no semantic test
